text: [serious] In December 1944, a young Japanese officer named Hiroo Onoda was sent to Lubang, a small island in the Philippines. His orders: keep fighting, and never surrender.
[serious] In December 1944, a young Japanese officer named Hiroo Onoda was sent to Lubang, a small island in the Philippines. His orders: keep fighting, and never surrender.
[serious] As American forces landed, his commander, Major Yoshimi Taniguchi, made him a promise. [softly] Whatever happens... we'll come back for you.

[softly] A few months later, World War Two ended. [sadly] But no one came.

[curious] Leaflets fell from planes saying the war was over. Onoda decided they were fake. Newspapers were left for him. Letters from his family. [sighs] He believed none of it.

[somber] So he stayed hidden in the jungle with a few other soldiers, still fighting his war.

[serious, quiet] And that war was real for the people of Lubang. Over the years, Onoda's group killed local islanders. As many as thirty, by some accounts.

[curious] Then, in 1974, a young Japanese traveler named Norio Suzuki arrived. He'd told friends he was searching for three things: Lieutenant Onoda, a panda, and the Abominable Snowman... in that order.

[serious] On March 9, 1974, Taniguchi stood in front of Onoda and read him his final orders. [softly] The war was over.
